acceptance_criteria.criterion: The Model Registry tab displays all registered models in a table with name, slug, and cc_model columns
The Add Model form auto-derives slug from name and generates a UUID `id` via `crypto.randomUUID()`
The slug field is editable for manual override despite auto-derivation
Client-side slug validation shows inline error messages for invalid format and reserved slug `"inherit"`; Save button is disabled while validation errors exist
Inline editing shows dirty indicators (colored dot) next to changed fields
Deleting a model shows a strikethrough on the row rather than removing it from the DOM
Saving sends the full model array to `PUT /api/models` and handles 409 (referenced model deletion) by displaying the error with a message directing to the Replace Model feature
"Load Defaults" shows a confirmation dialog, calls the API, and displays slug-collision conflicts if returned
The `cc_model` field includes helper text explaining its purpose
Client-side slug validation shows inline error messages for invalid format and reserved slug "inherit"; Save button is disabled while validation errors exist

summary: Replaced the Model Registry tab stub with a full implementation in mcp-server/gui/public/views/config.js. The tab maintains module-level state (mrModels / mrOriginal / mrEditingId) initialized from server data on first render. Features implemented: model table with name/slug/cc_model columns; inline row editing with Edit/Done/Cancel buttons; dirty indicator dots on changed fields (compared against the original server snapshot); strikethrough + Restore button for pending deletions (no immediate DOM removal); client-side slug validation against /^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$/ with reserved 'inherit' check and inline error messages; Save button disabled while validation errors exist; Add Model form with auto-slug derivation from name (tracks whether slug has been manually overridden), editable slug field, cc_model field with helper text, and crypto.randomUUID() for new model IDs; Save (PUT /api/models) with 409 conflict handling directing users to Replace Model on Persona Models tab; Load Defaults (POST /api/models/load-defaults) with confirmation dialog and slug-collision conflict display. Added corresponding CSS classes (.mr-dirty-dot, .mr-model-deleted, .mr-model-new, .mr-edit-row, .mr-field-error, .mr-error-text, .mr-add-section, .mr-action-bar) to styles.css. All 3523 existing tests pass; Node --check confirms no syntax errors.

comments.note: mrRefreshDirtyDots() is a documented no-op stub. During inline editing, dirty dots are only updated on full re-renders (triggered by Done/Cancel/action buttons), not on every keystroke. This means a dirty dot won't appear while a user is mid-edit until they press Done. A future improvement could update the dot in real-time during input events without a full re-render, e.g. by toggling a CSS class on the <td> directly.

The mrHasChanges() comparison in config.js uses index-based positional matching (mrModels[i] vs mrOriginal[i]) rather than ID-based matching. This is correct for the current bulk-save pattern where array order is stable, but would produce false positives if array reordering were ever added. A future refactor could switch to ID-keyed comparison.

The Add Model form's slug auto-derivation tracks 'previous value' via a custom property on the DOM input element (addNameInput._prevValue). This is a pragmatic workaround to avoid full re-renders on every keystroke, but it couples logic to DOM state. If the Add form were ever extracted into a component, this pattern would need to be replaced with explicit state tracking.

summary: All 9 acceptance criteria verified via static code analysis of config.js and styles.css. Node --check syntax validation passes. Full test suite runs clean: 3523 tests across 117 files pass with 0 failures, including 49 model-registry.test.ts and 36 api-models.test.ts targeted tests. All server-layer interactions (409 CONFLICT mapping, API.saveModels, API.loadDefaultModels) verified against api-models.ts and server.ts. Edge-case analysis: unsaved-changes guard correctly fires on tab navigation; state resets cleanly on page reload; empty-model-list, null-mrModels, and missing-response-key paths are all defensively handled. One low-priority observation noted regarding no unit tests for frontend helper functions (mrDeriveSlug, mrValidateSlug, mrHasChanges).

comments.note: The frontend helper functions mrDeriveSlug(), mrValidateSlug(), mrHasChanges(), and mrBuildTabHtml() in config.js have no dedicated unit tests. All are exercised indirectly via static code review and the backend api-models.test.ts suite (which covers the server-side equivalents). A future improvement could add a browser-environment (jsdom) test file that exercises these helpers directly, particularly the slug auto-derivation and dirty-comparison edge cases.

In-progress inline edits (typing in Edit row before clicking Done) are NOT reflected in configDirty.modelRegistry until Done is clicked. If a user switches tabs after editing a field but before clicking Done, those field edits are silently discarded without the unsaved-changes guard firing. The guard correctly fires for previously Done'd changes. This is an acceptable UX limitation — mid-edit field values are transient state, not committed to mrModels yet. Not an AC violation.

The 409 conflict error message in mrDoSave() references 'Replace Model' but the Persona Models tab is currently a stub ('Coming soon'). When the Persona Models tab is implemented (likely a future WP), the error message wording is already correct and will naturally become actionable.

summary: Full code review of the Model Registry tab implementation in config.js and styles.css. All 9 acceptance criteria confirmed met. Architecture is solid: module-level state (mrModels/mrOriginal/mrEditingId) is cleanly isolated; dirty comparison against mrOriginal snapshot is correct; bulk-save pattern is appropriate; XSS is guarded throughout (escapeHtml on all server data, textContent for validation errors). The mrBuildTabHtml/mrWireEvents split is maintainable. Server-side validation in model-registry.ts (Zod schema with name.min(1), slug regex, uuid, slug uniqueness, reserved slug guard, deletion guard) is comprehensive and provides a correct defence-in-depth backstop for any client-side gaps. One Fix-Forward applied: removed unused addBtn variable and void suppression in mrShowAddSlugError. Two Documentation-Forward items filed for the Documentation agent. PASS — no blocking issues found.

comments.note: mrShowAddSlugError (config.js ~line 656): Removed unused `addBtn` variable and `void addBtn` suppression statement. The variable was declared via getElementById but never used — the deliberate decision not to disable the Add button on slug error is correct behavior (validate on click), but the variable itself was dead code. Replaced with an explanatory comment. Non-behavioral change.

mrDoSave Done-row path (config.js ~line 463): `newName` is accepted without a client-side empty-name guard. If a user clears the Name field and clicks Done, the empty name is committed to mrModels and will cause a server-side 400 VALIDATION_ERROR on Save. The server's `name: z.string().min(1)` correctly rejects it, but a pre-Done client-side guard (`if (!newName) { nameInput.focus(); return; }`) would give earlier feedback. Not a blocker — server is authoritative.

No client-side duplicate-slug detection before Save. If a user adds a model with a slug that already exists in mrModels, the error surfaces only after a round-trip to the server (VALIDATION_ERROR). A pre-save check iterating mrModels for duplicate slugs would improve UX. Not a blocker — the server's slug-uniqueness guard is correct and authoritative.

[documentation-forward] mrRefreshDirtyDots() (config.js ~line 638) is a documented no-op stub. The module-level JSDoc or inline comment block should explain the deliberate design: dirty dots update on full re-renders (Done/Cancel/Delete/Restore) rather than on every keystroke, and mrRefreshDirtyDots is a hook reserved for future fine-grained optimisation. A future developer encountering calls to this function may incorrectly conclude it is broken or accidentally remove the calls.

[documentation-forward] The _prevValue custom DOM property on addNameInput (config.js ~line 587–592) tracks whether the slug has been manually diverged from the auto-derived value. This pattern is pragmatic but non-obvious. A comment immediately above the addNameInput.addEventListener block explaining why _prevValue exists (avoid full re-render on each keystroke while still tracking manual-vs-auto slug state) would help future maintainers.

notes: All 9 acceptance criteria met. The implementation is frontend-only (config.js + styles.css) — no backend changes were needed. Key design decisions: bulk-save pattern (local state accumulates all edits until Save); dirty comparison against mrOriginal snapshot; strikethrough-then-Restore deletion UX; auto-slug derivation only fires when the slug hasn't been manually diverged from the auto-derived value. The mrRefreshDirtyDots() function is intentionally a no-op stub — dot updates are handled by full re-renders on explicit actions (Done, Cancel, Delete, Restore, Save). QA should verify: (1) tab state resets correctly on page reload; (2) unsaved-changes guard triggers when navigating away with pending edits; (3) 409 error message renders correctly (requires a model referenced by a persona assignment to be marked for deletion before saving).

All 9 ACs confirmed. Implementation is clean and defensive. Frontend logic correctly chains: mrDeriveSlug → mrValidateSlug → dirty-indicator dots → bulk-save via PUT /api/models → 409 CONFLICT handling. The 3523-test suite passes with zero regressions. Key design notes for Reviewer: (1) mrRefreshDirtyDots() is a documented no-op stub — dots update on full re-renders only; (2) mrHasChanges() uses index-based positional comparison (correct for stable-order bulk-save); (3) _prevValue custom DOM property on the Add Name input tracks auto-slug derivation state — pragmatic but DOM-coupled. Three low-priority observations filed (no unit tests for frontend helpers, mid-edit tab-switch behavior, 409 message references future stub tab). None are blockers.

All 9 ACs confirmed met. Implementation is clean, well-commented, and architecturally sound.
